> Pick My Secret Santa is a free Secret Santa draw tool. Add names and a budget. It draws matches in secret, right in your browser.
> Each person gets a private link with their match, plus six gift ideas inside the budget. A private link is hidden from plain sight, not locked; anyone with a link can open it.
> Gift ideas come from a fixed list of 212 ideas. No ads, no accounts, no store links.

Frequently asked questions
How does this secret santa generator work?
Add every name and pick a budget.
No one draws their own name.
Each person gets one private link. That link shows just their match.
Do I need an email or an account?
No email or account is needed.
You send each private link yourself.
The site never emails or texts matches.
Can I keep some pairs apart?
Yes, you can mark pairs apart.
Mark pairs who must not draw each other.
The draw keeps marked pairs apart. Too many pairs can block the draw.
Can the organizer see who got whom?
Your screen shows names and links only. It never shows the matches.
Each match lives inside its private link.
A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked. Anyone with a link can open it.
Is this secret santa generator free?
Yes, the full draw is free. There is no sign-up at all.
There are no ads. Each person gets six gift ideas.

How many people do I need?
You need at least three people. Three is the smallest group that works.
Add a last initial for shared names.
Can I add someone after the draw?
Yes. You have two honest ways.
Draw the whole group again. Add the name first.
Every match is drawn fresh.
Send only the new set of links.
Old links still show the old draw.
No screen shows a match. The seal holds because nobody peeks.
Swap in a volunteer. One person gives up their match.
The new person takes that match.
The volunteer buys for the new person.
The old match gets a new Santa.
Three matches change. The group hears nothing.
The price: the volunteer tells you their match.
You set the swap up by hand.
So you learn those matches too.
One corner of the seal is spent.

When you swap gifts
Pick one game for the whole group.
Guess first.
Open one gift at a time, in turns. Guess your Santa first. Then they speak up.
Tag clue round.
One clue on the gift tag. The group guesses from the clue alone.
Three clues game.
Three clues, hard to easy. Guess after each one.
Note inside the wrap.
A signed note hidden in the wrapping. The outside stays blank.
Stand and point.
All Santas stand. Point at your guess. Santas sit when guessed right.
Balloon pop.
Pop a balloon after your gift. The name inside names your Santa.
Video reveal.
A short clip in a hat or a mask. Play the clips after the last gift.
All at once.
Every name told at once, after the last gift. A Santa can stay secret.

Keep it secret.
Want one for your group?
Start your own draw
Free. About 2 minutes.
Give it without giving yourself away
Pick the way that fits your place.
Desk drop.
Leave it on their desk before work starts. Slip away before they sit down. Best when you know their start time.
Doorstep drop.
Set the gift at their front door. Knock once, then walk away fast. Rain coming? Put it under cover first.
Front desk hold.
Leave it with the front desk or mail room. Ask staff to hand it over later. Put only their name on the label.
Helper handoff.
Ask a friend outside the game to deliver it. They say one line only: this is for you. Pick someone who will not spill the name.
Locker stash.
Slip it into their locker, cubby, or drawer. Use a spot they open every day. Make sure no one else can reach it.
Mailbox surprise.
Drop it in their work mailbox slot. Add a tag that says: open later, alone. Small, soft gifts fit this way best.
Plain mail box.
Mail it in a plain, sturdy box. Write no return name or address. Post it early. Holiday mail runs slow.
Clue trail.
Hide the gift somewhere safe nearby. Leave a first clue where they will see it. Each clue leads to the next one. The last clue leads to the gift.
Decoy box.
Put the gift inside a bigger, silly box. Wrap that box in plain paper. The odd shape hides what is inside. Add soft filler so nothing rattles.
Gift table drop.
Put it on the shared gift table early. Arrive before your person does. Then join the crowd like everyone else.
For every way: use plain wrap. Print the tag. Handwriting gives you away.
When you swap gifts
Pick one game for the whole group.
Guess first.
Open one gift at a time, in turns. Each person guesses their Santa first. Only then does the Santa speak up.
Tag clue round.
Write one clue on the gift tag. Read the tag aloud before opening. The group guesses from the clue alone.
Three clues game.
Each Santa gives three clues, one by one. Clues start hard and get easier. The person guesses after each clue.
Note inside the wrap.
Hide a signed note inside the wrapping paper. Your person finds it while they open. Keep the outside of the gift blank.
Stand and point.
After the last gift, all Santas stand up. Each person points at their best guess. Santas sit down when guessed right.
Balloon pop.
Put each Santa name inside a balloon. Each person pops one after opening their gift. The name inside names their Santa.
Video reveal.
Film a short clip before the party. Start in a hat or a mask. Take it off and say your name. Play the clips after the last gift.
All at once.
Tell everyone at once after the last gift. No guessing, no games, all names together. A Santa can stay secret if they want.
This link does not work.
Ask your organizer for a fresh one.
Only trust a link your organizer sent you.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/privacy

Privacy - Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Privacy
The short version:
Names and the draw stay in your browser. Cloudflare Web Analytics counts visits here. PostHog counts draws, shares, and link opens, as counts only. There are no accounts here.
What the draw does
You type names, a budget, and any pairs who should not draw each other.
The draw math runs in your browser.
Nothing you type on this site is sent to us.
Say what a person is into, in your words.
In the draw tool, those words are matched on this device, and they are not sent or saved.
No name is asked for there.
If you use the Ask panel instead, your words go to this site's AI, which reads them and picks from the site's gift list.
Nothing you type in the Ask panel is saved.
After a draw, your browser saves your links.
They stay on this device only.
That way you can send a link again later.
You can clear them any time with two taps.
On a shared device, clear them when done.
Private links
Each link holds one person's match.
The match sits inside the link itself.
Our server never sees the match.
A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked.
Anyone with a link can open it.
Send each link only to its person.
You share links with your own apps.
Sharing starts only when you tap a button.
How visits are counted
This site loads Cloudflare Web Analytics.
It sends page and performance counts to Cloudflare.
Cloudflare says its beacon uses no cookies.
This site also loads PostHog.
PostHog counts page views, draws, shares, link opens, and card saves.
Gift idea matches count as a count of picks only.
It also counts return visits.
Start your own draw taps count too.
It counts actions only, never what you type.
No names, matches, gift picks, or link parts are sent.
PostHog sets no cookie on this site.
Your browser keeps one yes-or-no mark on this device.
It says this browser has drawn or peeked before.
It holds no names, matches, gift picks, or links.
It lets a later visit count as a return visit.
Your saved draw stays on this device too.
It holds your names and each person's link.
It is never sent to us or to PostHog.
Counts never include anything inside it.
The ChatGPT plugin
Pick My Secret Santa also runs as a plugin inside ChatGPT.
In the chat, you set the group up in words.
The chat does the talking. The draw still runs here, in your browser.
The plugin never draws and never assigns anyone.
If you give the chat your group's names, they pass through our server once.
They are held in memory only, to build your pre-filled link.
They are never stored.
Our server counts plugin tool calls by day, as counts only.
The names also stay in your chat history.
That history is kept under ChatGPT's rules, not ours.
Children
Adults run the draws on this site.
Some gifts here are for children.
It is not directed at children under 13.
Contact
Questions about privacy: hello@pickmysecretsanta.com.
Changes
Changes will appear on this page.

Terms - Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Terms
These terms cover this website and its ChatGPT plugin.
This site is a free Secret Santa tool.
You add names and a budget.
It draws matches and suggests gifts.
There are no ads on this site.
There are no accounts or sign-ups.
The site sells nothing at all.
How the draw works
The draw is random, with two rules.
Nobody draws their own name.
Pairs you mark never draw each other.
The draw runs in your browser.
We never see your group's matches.
Some rule sets cannot form a draw.
The site will say so when that happens.
The ChatGPT plugin
The plugin sets a group up inside ChatGPT.
It hands back one pre-filled link to this site.
It never draws or assigns anyone.
The draw happens here, in your browser.
Names given in chat pass through our server in memory only.
They build the link and are never stored.
What you type in chat also sits in your chat history.
That history is kept under ChatGPT's rules.
Where gift ideas come from
Gift ideas come from a fixed list.
The list is Santa's 212, from the shared 255-idea bank it shares with The Present Picker.
Your budget is a hard filter.
A gift hint raises matching ideas.
Budget bands are guides, not exact prices.
Stores set real prices, and prices change.
Buying your gift
This site links to no stores.
It takes no payment from you.
It places no orders for you.
You choose where and what to buy.
Check each idea before you buy.
Accounts and data
Names and draws stay in your browser.
Cloudflare Web Analytics counts visits here.
PostHog counts draws, shares, and link opens.
It also counts return visits. All as counts only.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/how-does-secret-santa-work

How Does Secret Santa Work? — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
How does Secret Santa work?
One gift each. One name each. No screen shows who has whom. Matches stay hidden until the swap.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
1Agree a budget
2Draw a name
3Buy one gift
4Swap day
The short version
Secret Santa is a group gift swap with the names hidden.
Agree a budget. One number everyone can afford.
Draw one name each. Your name is the only one you see.
Buy one gift. For your person only, inside the budget.
Swap on the day. Wrapped, labeled with their name, never yours.
That is the whole game. The secret is the fun part.
The rules most groups use
At least three people. Two is just a trade.
No one draws their own name. If it happens, draw again.
Label the gift with their name only.
Stay secret until the swap. Guessing is half the party.
Run it with this site
The draw runs in your browser. Nothing is sent to a server.
Name your group. Pick a gift budget.
Add every name. Add what each person likes.
Mark pairs to keep apart. Only if some must not draw each other.
Tap Draw the names. Each person gets one private link.
Send each link to its person only. The link shows just their match.
Each person also gets six gift ideas that fit the budget.
How the online draw works
Ways groups bend it
Keep some pairs apart. Couples and close family often sit the draw out for each other. Mark the pairs before you draw.
Add someone late. Draw the whole group again and the seal stays whole. Or a volunteer gives up their match, and the site names the price out loud: the volunteer tells the organizer their match. Both ways, in full.
White elephant is a cousin, not the same game. There, gifts are swapped and stolen in the open. Secret Santa is one secret match, bought for one person.
Reveal games. End the swap with a guessing game. See all eight reveal games.
Common questions
How many people do we need?
At least three. Three is the smallest group that works.
Can the organizer peek at the matches?
The screen itself does not show them. It shows names and links only.
Each match lives inside its private link.
The organizer holds every link and could open one. A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked. The seal is that the organizer does not peek.
What budget is normal?
Any one number the whole group can afford.
Most groups land between $10 and $30. Say the number before the draw.
What if someone forgets their person?
Their link still works. Links stay saved on the organizer device too.
The organizer can send the same link again.
Ready when you are
Start your draw

How to Run a Secret Santa — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
How to run a Secret Santa
The organiser's short list. Set it up once, then let the draw do the hiding.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
1Set day and budget
2Add names
3Draw and send links
4Swap and guess
The run, step by step
Pick the swap day. Agree one gift budget.
Collect every name, and what each person likes.
Add the names here. Mark pairs to keep apart.
Tap Draw the names. Send each private link to its person only.
Post the sealed receipt in the group chat.
On swap day, end with a guessing game.
Before the draw
Set a buy-by date. A week before the swap works for most groups.
Say the budget early. One number, the whole group, no exceptions.
Ask what each person likes. The tool takes likes in your own words, on step 2.
Ask about pairs. Mark them on step 3.
While you send the links
Send the group message first. It carries the budget and the rules.
Then send each private link to its person only.
Your share screen counts the links as you send them.
It names who still needs theirs, on this device only.
Closed the tab? Your draw stays saved on this device.
Open the site again and send the missing link.
On swap day
Each gift is labeled with one name: the person it is for.
Nobody signs their own name.
End with a reveal game, and let the group guess.
See the eight reveal games
Keep planning
How Secret Santa works: the game in four steps.
How to run a Secret Santa: the organiser's short list.
Secret Santa rules: the classic rules, plus the enforced ones.
Gift ideas under $50: real picks, by interest.
Secret Santa for large groups: one draw for up to 30 people.
Common questions
How long does it take to run a draw?
About two minutes to set up. Sending the links takes as long as your own messages take.
What if someone joins late?
Draw the whole group again, so the seal stays whole. Or swap in a volunteer, who gives up their match and tells the organiser.
How do I prove the draw was fair?
Post the sealed receipt to the group. It shows the group, the date, the names, and the budget. It shows no matches and no links.

Secret Santa Rules — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Secret Santa rules
The short list most groups play by, plus the rules the draw here enforces for you.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
3+people in the group
1budget for everyone
The classic rules
At least three people. Two is just a trade.
One budget. Agreed before the draw, the same for everyone.
One name each. Each person draws one name, never their own.
One gift. Bought for your person only, inside the budget.
Their name on the gift.
Secret until the swap. Guessing is half the party.
Rules this site enforces
No one draws their own name. The draw cannot deal it, ever.
Marked pairs stay apart. Pairs you mark never draw each other.
Impossible draws stop early. If the pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so. Nobody gets a link until the draw works.
One link per person. Each private link shows one match only.
Four budgets. Under $25, $25 to $50, $50 to $100, and over $100.
Agree these out loud
A buy-by date. The draw cannot set one for you.
What counts as the gift. Bought, made, or regifted? Say it first.
Late joiners. Decide now: draw again, or swap in a volunteer. Both ways, in full.
The reveal. Guess first, or open in turns? Pick one before the day.
The honest edges
With three people, one match gives away the rest.
With four people and pairs marked, one match can give away another.
A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked.
Anyone with a link can open it. Send each link to its person only.
A new draw makes new links. Links from the old draw still work.

What are the basic Secret Santa rules?
At least three people. One budget everyone can afford. Each person draws one name, never their own. Buy one gift inside the budget. Label it with their name only, and stay secret until the swap.
Can someone draw their own name here?
No. The draw here cannot give anyone their own name. If marked pairs make a draw impossible, the site says so before any link is made.
What happens when we draw again?
A new draw makes new links. Links from the old draw still work, and they show the old matches. Send only the new set.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/white-elephant-vs-secret-santa

White Elephant vs Secret Santa — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
White elephant vs Secret Santa
One game buys for a person. The other game fights over a pile.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
Secret Santa
One secret match. One gift for one named person.
White elephant
No names. Gifts sit in a pile, stolen in the open.
Side by side
Who gets the gift? Secret Santa: one named person. White elephant: whoever ends holding it.
How are names picked? Secret Santa: drawn in secret, one match each. White elephant: no names at all.
How do gifts move? Secret Santa: wrapped, labeled with their name only. White elephant: picked from a pile, then stolen in turns.
What stays secret? Secret Santa: who bought your gift, until the swap. White elephant: only what hides inside the wrap.
Where does it work? Secret Santa: any group, near or far. White elephant: one room, one pile, one crowd.
Pick your game
Pick Secret Santa when each gift should fit its person.
Pick Secret Santa when your group is spread out.
Pick white elephant when the stealing is the whole party.
Pick white elephant when gag gifts beat thoughtful ones.
The honest part
This site runs Secret Santa only.
It draws one secret match per person, in your browser.
It does not run a white elephant pile.
If your group picks white elephant, you need no draw at all.
Just set one budget, wrap the gifts, and gather in one room.
Keep planning
Secret Santa at work: one draw for the whole team.
How much to spend on Secret Santa: the four budgets, compared.
White elephant vs Secret Santa: two games, one clear winner per group.
How Secret Santa works: the game in four steps.
How to run a Secret Santa: the organiser's short list.
Secret Santa rules: the classic rules, plus the enforced ones.
Secret Santa for large groups: one draw for up to 30 people.
Common questions
What is the main difference?
Secret Santa buys one gift for one named person, in secret. White elephant puts wrapped gifts in a pile, and players pick and steal in the open.
Which game does this site run?
This site runs Secret Santa only. It draws one secret match per person. It does not run a white elephant pile or stealing rounds.
Which game suits a remote group?
Secret Santa. Each person gets a private link, so the draw works when the group never shares a room. White elephant needs everyone in one place, watching the pile.
Can a group play both?
Yes, on different days. Run the secret draw for real gifts first. Save the pile game for the party itself.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/can-you-add-someone-to-secret-santa-after-the-draw

Can You Add Someone to Secret Santa After the Draw — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Can you add someone to Secret Santa after the draw
Yes. Two honest ways, and what each one costs.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
Way one: draw again
Every secret kept. The cost is new links.
Way two: a volunteer swaps
One secret spent: the volunteer tells you their match.
The short answer
Yes, someone can join after the draw.
There are two honest ways, and only two.
Way one keeps every secret. Draw the whole group again.
Way two spends one secret. A volunteer swaps their match.
There is no way to add just one link to a finished draw.
Way one: draw the whole group again
Add the new name to the group.
Draw the whole group again.
Every match is drawn fresh.
Send only the new set of links.
Old links still show the old draw.
The seal stays whole. This way costs no secret at all.
Tell the group only that the draw ran again.
Way two: swap in a volunteer
One person gives up their match.
The new person takes that match.
The volunteer buys for the new person instead.
The old match gets a new Santa.
Three matches change. The group hears nothing.
The price: the volunteer tells you their match.
You set the swap up by hand, so you learn those matches too.
One corner of the seal is spent.
Which way fits
Nobody has bought a gift yet? Way one. It costs nothing but new links.
Gifts are bought and links are out? Way two. Only three matches move.
Nobody will volunteer? Back to way one. Those are the two honest ways.
New to running one? Read how to run a Secret Santa.
Keep planning

Common questions
Can I just add one more link?
No. A finished draw has no way to add one link. Pick one of the two ways on this page instead.
If we draw again, do the old links stop working?
No. Links you already sent still work and show the old draw. Send only the new set, so nobody follows an old match.
Does the volunteer way break the secret?
Partly. The volunteer tells the organiser their match, and the organiser learns those matches too. The rest of the group hears nothing.
How many matches change in the volunteer swap?
Three matches change. The group hears nothing about which three.

How Many People Do You Need for Secret Santa — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
How many people do you need for Secret Santa
Three is the smallest group that works.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
3people is the smallest group that works. One draw here holds up to 30.
The answer first
At least three people.
Up to 30 in one draw here.
More than 30? Split the group into smaller draws.
The draw asks for at least three names. Fewer, and it will not run.
Why two does not work
Two is just a trade.
Each person would know exactly who has them.
There is no secret left to keep.
Buy each other a gift and call it what it is.
Three works, with one honest edge
Three people can draw, and nobody draws their own name.
Each person gets one private link with one match.
The edge, in plain words: with three people, one match gives away the rest.
Once you know your match, the other two fall into place.
Four or more keeps the secret stronger.
With four people and pairs marked, one match can give away another.
That edge is printed on the Secret Santa rules page too.
Bigger groups
That range covers most teams, classes, and clubs.
A bigger group splits into smaller draws.
Split by team, by class, or by table.
Each draw is its own game, with its own receipt.
Nobody crosses between draws.
Running a big one? Read Secret Santa for large groups.
Small group tips that the draw supports
Shared first names? Add a last initial for shared names.
Pairs to keep apart? Mark them before the draw.
Too many pairs? The draw can block. If the pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so.
One budget for everyone. Under $25, $25 to $50, $50 to $100, or over $100.
Each person gets six gift ideas inside that budget.

Secret Santa Generator With Exclusions — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Secret Santa generator with exclusions
Mark the pairs. The draw keeps them apart.

Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
1Mark the pairs
2Tap Draw the names
3Marked pairs stay apart
The answer first
Yes, pairs stay apart. Mark pairs who must not draw each other.
Every pair is honored. A marked pair is never dealt by the draw.
Too many pairs can block the draw.
No one draws their own name either. That rule is built in, always.
Run the draw with exclusions
Name your group. Pick a gift budget.
Add every name. Add what each person likes.
Mark each pair who must not draw each other.
Add another pair, or remove one, any time before the draw.
Tap Draw the names. The draw keeps marked pairs apart.
Send each private link to its person only.
Each person opens their link and sees one match, plus six gift ideas.
Who groups keep apart
Couples and partners. Two people who already buy for each other.
People who share a home. A surprise is hard to hide under one roof.
Last year's matches. Mark them apart, and nobody draws the same person twice.
One pair takes two names. Add as many pairs as the group needs.
The step is optional. Most groups can skip it and draw at once.
The honest edges
Three people and one pair. With three people, one pair apart leaves no fair draw.
The site says so before any link is made. Its words: That draw cannot work.
Remove one pair you marked, and the draw runs.
Four people and pairs. With four people and pairs marked, one match can give away another.
The receipt proves it. The sealed receipt names how many pairs were kept apart.
It shows no matches and no links. Post it to the whole group.
The full rule list: Secret Santa rules.

Can You Resend a Secret Santa Link — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Can you resend a Secret Santa link
Yes. Your last draw stays saved on this device.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
1draw saved on this device
0links kept on a server
2taps to clear the saved draw
The answer first
Yes, from this device. Your last draw is saved on this device.
Nothing sits on a server.
Send a link again any time. Send a link again, or share the receipt.
Close this tab, come back, and send a link again.
How resending works
Open this site on the device that ran the draw.
Find Your saved draw at the top of the page.
The saved list shows one card per person.
Each card names only its owner, outside its link.
Send that person's link again, to its person only.
The link still shows their true match.
Not sure who still needs one? The share screen names who still needs theirs.
The honest limits
Only the newest draw is saved.
Same device, same browser. The list lives in this browser, on this device.
A different device has no saved draw to send from.
Anyone on this device can open the links.
On a shared device, clear the draw when done.
Clearing takes two taps. Clear the saved draw any time.
Sent links keep working. Links you already sent still work, even after you clear.
Why the links live here and nowhere else: Can the organizer see who got whom.
Lost your link?
Ask your organizer for a fresh one.
Only trust a link your organizer sent you.
Your organizer sees names and links only, never the matches.
Sending your link again shows them nothing new.
This link does not work? Ask your organizer for a fresh one.

Common questions
Can you resend a Secret Santa link?
Yes. Your last draw is saved on this device. Send a link again, or share the receipt. Nothing is saved on our server.
What if I close the tab?
Your links stay saved on this device. Open this page again to send one. Nothing is saved on our server. Clear your saved draw any time.
Someone lost their link. What now?

Can I resend from a different phone or computer?
No. The saved draw lives on the device that ran the draw. On this site, our server never sees your names or links, so there is nothing to fetch.

Links you already sent still work. To send one again, run the draw again. A new draw makes new links. Send only the new set.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/secret-santa-generator

Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws names in secret.
Secret Santa generator
Say six coworkers join in. You add six names. You pick a $25 budget. The draw pairs each person once. Nobody draws their own name. Each person gets one private link. The link shows one match only.
51 days until Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Run your draw in five steps
Step What you do
1 Name your group. Pick a gift budget.
2 Add every name. Add likes too.
3 Mark pairs to keep apart.
4 Tap Draw the names. It runs here.
5 Send each private link yourself.
The draw runs in your browser. Our server never sees your names. Each link shows one match only. It also shows six gift ideas. All six sit inside your budget.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Is this Secret Santa generator free?
Yes. The full draw is free. There is no sign-up. There are no ads. You send each link yourself.
How many people can join one draw?
One draw holds 3 to 30 people. Bigger groups split by team. Each team runs its own draw.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/gift-exchange-name-draw

Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws names in secret.
Gift exchange name draw
Say your family swaps gifts. Eight names go into the draw. The draw pairs each name once. You mark partners apart first. Each person gets one private link. Nobody sees the full list. Each link shows one match only.
51 days until Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
How the draw keeps it fair
Rule How the draw keeps it
No self draws Nobody ever draws their own name.
Pairs apart Marked pairs never draw each other.
One link each Each link shows one match only.
No full list No screen shows every match together.
Add at least three names. One draw holds up to 30. Pick a budget before you draw. Then send each link yourself. The draw runs in your browser.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Is a name draw the same game?
Yes. A gift exchange is Secret Santa. One name drawn in secret. One gift bought for that person.
What if no fair draw exists?
The draw says so first. No links get made. Loosen one marked pair. Then draw again right away.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/dirty-santa-rules

Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws names in secret.
Dirty Santa rules
Dirty Santa is a swap with steals. Each guest brings one wrapped gift. The group sets one price cap first. You open gifts in turn. A turn can end with a steal.
51 days until Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
The rules, step by step
Bring one wrapped gift near the budget.
Write one number per slip. All draw one slip.
Number one picks a wrapped gift. They open it for all to see.
The next guest makes a choice. Open a new gift, or steal an opened one.
If your gift gets stolen, pick once more. Open a fresh one, or steal one back.
Most groups cap steals on one gift. Three steals in a round is the norm.
Play ends when every gift stands open.
Number one takes the last move. They may swap for any opened gift.
House rules bend these steps. Set the steal cap first. That one call stops most fights.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Is Dirty Santa the same as White Elephant?
Nearly. The name shifts from place to place. The steal game stays the same.
How is Dirty Santa not Secret Santa?
Secret Santa gives each guest one name in secret. This game fights for gifts in the open. No names get drawn at all.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/can-you-do-secret-santa-with-an-odd-number-of-people

Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws names in secret.
Can you do Secret Santa with an odd number of people?
Yes. Odd numbers work fine. The draw is a ring. Each person gives to one person and gets from one person. Odd or even never enters into it.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Why the ring always closes
Every name goes in once. Every name gets drawn once. No one draws their own name — the draw cannot deal it, ever. With 5, 7, or 9 people, the ring still closes. Nobody is left out, and nobody is left over.
The only real floor is three
Two people cannot play — each would know the other's match. Three works, with one honest edge: one match can give away the rest. After three, any number works, odd or even.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Does an odd number leave someone without a gift?
No. Each person draws exactly one name, and each name is drawn exactly once. The count of givers always equals the count of gifts.
Can pairs change the math?
You can mark pairs to keep apart, like partners. If the pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so before anyone gets a link.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/what-if-someone-drops-out-of-secret-santa

Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws names in secret.
What if someone drops out of Secret Santa?
It is fixable — if gifts are not bought yet. The clean fixes are the same two as adding someone late: draw the whole group again, or swap in a volunteer.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Way one: draw the whole group again
Take the name out and run the draw again. Everyone gets a new link. A new draw makes new links — and links from the old draw still work, so send the new ones and say plainly that the old ones are dead.
Way two: a volunteer swaps
One person agrees to give to the person who lost their Santa. Nobody else's match changes. This works best in small groups, where a full redraw feels like a big deal.
Tell the organizer early
Both fixes get harder once gifts are bought. If you must drop out, say so the day you know. Your own link just goes unused — it reveals nothing about anyone else.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
We already drew. Now what?
Draw again, or swap in a volunteer. It is the same pair of fixes as adding someone after the draw.
What if their Santa already bought a gift?
Then it is the group's call. The gift can still be given at the swap. Most groups would rather get the gift than follow the rule.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/do-you-reveal-who-your-secret-santa-was

Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws names in secret.
Do you reveal who your secret santa was?
Most groups do — at the swap, after the gifts open. The name stays secret until then. Guessing who gave what is half the party.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Pick one reveal game before the day
This site offers reveal games for the swap: Guess first , Three clues , and Balloon pop . Five more games show in your link at the swap. Pick one before the day, so the end of the party has a plan.
Or open in turns
The other classic: each person opens, then guesses out loud before the giver owns up. Either way, the reveal comes last — after every gift is open.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Do we have to reveal?
No. It is your group's call. Some groups never reveal. Most do, because the guessing is the fun part.
When do we reveal?
At the swap, after the gift opens. Secret until the swap is the rule the whole game rests on.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/how-to-do-secret-santa-with-family

Pick My Secret Santa

How to do Secret Santa with family
One draw for the whole family. Each person buys one gift, for one person, inside one budget the whole family agrees on. Names stay secret until the swap.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
The family run, step by step
Pick the gift exchange day. Agree one gift budget — most groups land between $10 and $30, and one number for everyone keeps it fair. Collect every name, and what each person likes. Add the names here. Mark pairs to keep apart — partners, say, or the same household. Tap Draw the names. Send each private link to its person only. On the day, end with a guessing game.
Kids can play too
The draw's bank holds 60 kid picks, so a child in the draw still gets ideas that fit. Set a buy-by date — a week before the exchange works for most groups — so nobody is shopping on the day.
Family far away?
Distance does not end the game. Run the same draw online and swap by mail or on a call — see Virtual Secret Santa .
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Can kids play with the grown-ups?
Yes. Kids go in the same draw. The bank's kid picks mean their link still deals six ideas inside the budget.
What budget is fair for a family?
Any one number the whole group can afford. Most groups land between $10 and $30. Say the number before the draw.

Secret Santa for small groups
Small groups work. Three is the smallest group that works. Four or five keeps the secret stronger. One draw, one budget, and each person gets one private link with one match.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
A real small draw, from this site's own sample
Four friends in. Four private links out. Each match stays sealed in its own link. Inside Maya's link — only Maya sees this — she got Tom, with six gift ideas inside the budget. The organizer's screen shows the names and the links, never who got whom.
The honest edge of three
Three people can draw, and nobody draws their own name. The edge, in plain words: with three people, one match gives away the rest. Once you know your match, the other two fall into place. With four people and pairs marked, one match can give away another. Four or more keeps the secret stronger.
Small group tips the draw supports
Shared first names? Add a last initial. Pairs to keep apart? Mark them before the draw — if the pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so. One budget for everyone, and pick the reveal game before the day.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.

At least three people. Up to 30 in one draw here. Two is just a trade — each person would know exactly who has them.
Can pairs change the math?

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/when-to-start-secret-santa

Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws names in secret.
When should you start Secret Santa?
Start when your group can agree two things: one budget and one gift day. The draw itself takes about 2 minutes, any day you run it. The buying needs the lead time — this site's rule is a buy-by date a week before gift day.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
The order that works, from the site's own run list
Pick the gift exchange day. Agree one gift budget — most groups land between $10 and $30. Collect every name, and what each person likes. Run the draw and send each private link to its person only. Set the buy-by date a week before the exchange, so nobody is shopping on the day.
Gifts going by mail? Start earlier
Mail each gift in a plain box, early. Holiday mail runs slow. Agree the mail-by day before anyone buys — the day is the group's to set, and this site holds no date for you.
Christmas this year
Christmas Day is Friday, December 25, 2026. The countdown at the top of this page counts the days in your own time zone. A buy-by date a week before gift day lands a week before the day your group picks.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
How late can we start?
The draw takes about 2 minutes, so the draw is never the slow part. Leave room to buy: a week before gift day is the buy-by rule this site gives its own sample draw.
When is Christmas in 2026?
Friday, December 25, 2026. The countdown on this page shows the days left where you are.

Secret Santa for remote teams
One draw for the whole team, wherever they work. No accounts for anyone. No sign-up, no work email needed. Each person opens a private link, mails one gift, and the team opens them together on one video call.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
The remote run, step by step
Agree one budget and one mail-by day. Add every name, from three to thirty people. Mark pairs who must not draw each other. Draw the names in your browser. Send each person their own private link — a link opens anywhere, any town, any time zone. Mail each gift in a plain, sturdy box, early. Meet on a video call and open together.
Why it works spread out
The draw runs in your browser. No names reach a server. Gift ideas come with the match — each person gets six ideas inside the budget. Remote and in-room mix fine, so a hybrid team plays as one group.
Reveal on the call
Video reveal fits a call. Each Santa films a short clip first. Start in a hat or a mask. Take it off and say your name. Play the clips after the last gift is opened. Guess first works too.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Does the site email my team for me?
No. The site never emails or texts anyone. You send each private link yourself, in the chat or mail thread your team already uses.
How many people can join one remote draw?
One draw holds 3 to 30 people. A bigger team splits into smaller draws, one per group or floor.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/do-you-put-your-name-on-a-secret-santa-gift

Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws names in secret.
Do you put your name on a Secret Santa gift?
No. Their name only. The classic rule: put their name on the gift, and nothing of yours. You stay secret until the swap — guessing who gave what is half the party.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
What goes on the gift
The rules this site prints are short: their name on the gift. Secret until the swap. At the swap, each person opens, then guesses out loud before the giver owns up — that is when your name comes out, in person, not on the tag.
Mailing it? Keep the box plain too
Mail it in a plain, sturdy box. Write no return name or address. A name on the box gives the game away before the party starts.
Pick the reveal before the day
Groups here pick one reveal game before the day: Guess first, Three clues, or Balloon pop. The reveal comes last — after every gift is open.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
What are the basic Secret Santa rules?
At least three people. One budget everyone can afford. Each person draws one name, never their own. Buy one gift inside the budget. Label it with their name only, and stay secret until the swap.
Do we have to reveal at the end?
No. It is your group's call. Some groups never reveal. Most do, because the guessing is the fun part.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/what-if-you-draw-your-own-name-in-secret-santa

Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws names in secret.
What if you draw your own name in Secret Santa?
Here, it cannot happen. No one draws their own name. The draw cannot deal it, ever. That rule is built in, always — it is not a setting you have to turn on.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
In a paper draw: draw again
The classic rules this site prints are short: each person draws one name, never their own. If it happens with names in a hat, draw again. That is the whole fix, and every group plays it that way.
What this draw does instead
The draw runs in your browser and deals one private link per person. Each link shows one match only, and a match is never the person's own name. If marked pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so before any link is made — nobody gets a link until the draw works.
Pairs are the one edge to watch
With three people, one match gives away the rest. With four people and pairs marked, one match can give away another. Four or more, with no tight pairs, keeps the secret stronger.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Can someone draw their own name here?
No. The draw here cannot give anyone their own name. If marked pairs make a draw impossible, the site says so before any link is made.
What happens when we draw again?
A new draw makes new links. Links from the old draw still work, and they show the old matches. Send only the new set.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/can-couples-do-secret-santa

Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws names in secret.
Can couples do Secret Santa?
Yes. Couples play like everyone else — and the draw can keep them apart. Mark the two names as one pair before the draw. Neither of them can draw the other. Every pair you mark is honored.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Why groups keep couples apart
Two people who already buy for each other get no surprise from drawing each other. People who share a home have the same problem — a surprise is hard to hide under one roof. The exclusions page lists both as the pairs groups keep apart most, along with last year's matches.
How to mark a pair
Name your group. Pick a gift budget. Add every name. Mark each pair who must not draw each other — one pair takes two names, and you can add as many pairs as the group needs. Tap Draw the names. Send each private link to its person only.
The honest edges
Too many pairs can block the draw. With three people, one pair apart leaves no fair draw — the site says so before any link is made, in its own words: that draw cannot work. Remove one pair you marked, and the draw runs. With four people and pairs marked, one match can give away another.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Can couples or partners be kept apart?
Yes. Mark the two names as one pair before the draw. Neither of them can draw the other.
What if the pairs leave no fair draw?
If the pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so before any link is made. Remove one pair you marked, and draw again.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/how-to-give-a-secret-santa-gift-anonymously

Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws names in secret.
How to give a Secret Santa gift anonymously
Their name only — and hand it over where you are not seen. Label the gift with their name, and nothing of yours. For every way below: use plain wrap, and print the tag. Handwriting gives you away.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Four ways to hand it over at work
Desk drop: leave it on their desk before work starts, and slip away before they sit down. Front desk hold: leave it with the front desk or mail room, with only their name on the label. Mailbox surprise: drop it in their work mailbox slot — small, soft gifts fit this way best. Gift table drop: put it on the shared gift table early, and arrive before your person does.
Sending it by mail instead?
Mail it in a plain, sturdy box. Write no return name or address — a name on the box gives the game away before the party starts. Post it early. Holiday mail runs slow.
Stay secret until the swap
The classic rule: secret until the swap. At the swap, each person opens, then guesses out loud before the giver owns up. That is when your name comes out — in person, not on the tag.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Do you put your name on a Secret Santa gift?
No. Their name only. Put their name on the gift, and nothing of yours. You stay secret until the swap.
How do I mail a Secret Santa gift without giving myself away?
Use a plain, sturdy box and write no return name or address. Mail it early — holiday mail runs slow.

I forgot who my Secret Santa is
Open your link again. It still works. Your private link shows your true match, and links you were sent keep working. Forgot is fixable — nobody has to redraw for one lost name.

Start your draw
Lost the link itself?

The honest limits
Only the newest draw is saved, on the same device, in the same browser. A different phone or computer has no saved draw to send from. Nothing sits on a server — the draw runs in the browser, and our server never sees your names or your matches.
Forgot who has you, instead?
That one stays secret on purpose. The organizer's screen shows names and links only, never the matches. Each match lives inside its private link only. Guessing is half the party — that answer comes at the swap, not before.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/can-you-swap-secret-santa-names

Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws names in secret.
Can you swap Secret Santa names?
Not one match by itself. A finished draw has no way to edit or swap just one name. There are two honest ways, and only two — the same two this site gives for adding someone late or fixing a drop-out.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Way one: draw the whole group again
Every secret kept. Draw the whole group again, and every match is drawn fresh. Send only the new set of links — old links still show the old draw. Tell the group only that the draw ran again. Nobody has bought a gift yet? This is the way. It costs nothing but new links.
Way two: a volunteer swaps
One person gives up their match, and takes the other match instead. Three matches change, and the group hears nothing. The price, named out loud: the volunteer tells the organizer their match, and the organizer learns those matches too. One corner of the seal is spent. Gifts are bought and links are out? This is the way.
Someone dropped out instead?
Same pair of fixes. Draw again with the name taken out, or a volunteer gives to the person who lost their Santa. Both fixes get harder once gifts are bought — say so the day you know.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. The seal is trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Can I just swap one match?
No. A finished draw has no way to swap or edit one match. Pick one of the two ways on this page instead.
Does the volunteer way break the secret?
Partly. The volunteer tells the organiser their match, and the organiser learns those matches too. The rest of the group hears nothing.
